provenance: PR #41 R4, closing the half of T-R51 its own acceptance asked for and the labelling route did not ship. T-R51 said 'Watched red either way'. The route taken — CI's wall clocks are hand-read off the log of a named workflow run rather than committed to the ledger — landed with nothing that could go red, and ADR-019 §5 admitted it in those words: 'Nothing grades the four measurements'. Editing README's `74.04` to `99.99` left `--suite invariant` at 60/60 = 1.000. T-R51's own 'Compounding' clause was this same defect one version earlier: README published the CI band twice, in two incompatible forms (59.77 / 60.84 / 64.61 / 64.67s beside 69.37-74.06s), with 64.61 sitting in this repo's ledger as a LOCAL run — two documents drifting because one source was retyped into both. This gives the CI numbers the same contract `published-band-matches-the-ledger` item 7 (readme-row) already gives README's LOCAL band row: ADR-019 §5's attempt table is the ONE source, README's four `fast` values and both min-max ranges are read back FROM it rather than compared against literals typed into the check, the run id that makes them reader-checkable appears in both documents, and the ceilings §5 derives from its own maxima are the ones `.github/workflows/eval.yml` declares — which closes the chain table -> ADR-013's rule -> workflow, the thing the four numbers exist to justify. Deliberately NOT graded, because it cannot be from here: that anyone ever measured those four numbers. The run id is what a reader checks with `gh run view 32561162459 --attempt N --log`; this case only refuses the two documents drifting apart and a run id no document mentions. Same reason no CI row reaches the ledger (T-R73). The regexes are function-local rather than module-level because ADR-019 §6 enumerates the module-level names its band region does not pin, and a new constant there would have made that enumeration stale — the defect class §6 exists for.

triage.note: tagged invariant and fast, like the rest of the band/ceiling documentation guards. Pure code: three file reads and a regex, no network, no spend. It reads `.github/workflows/eval.yml`, which `fast-wall-clock-budget` also parses — that case pins the values the workflow declares, this one pins that those values are what ADR-019 §5's own table derives, so neither subsumes the other. What it does NOT cover: whether the measurements are real (unknowable locally, T-R73), and any CI figure published outside ADR-019 §5 and README — ADR-013's copy of the superseded 95-case band is owned by `task/T-M32-9` and is out of this branch's scope (PR #41 R3).

One false start worth recording: the first version searched `eval-gate run (\\d{6,})` and reported `names_no_workflow_run_for_the_ci_numbers` against a document that names it — ADR-019 §5 wraps the id onto the next line inside a markdown link. Fixed to tolerate the wrap, the same allowance `_SIX_REF` already makes for slugs near a line end; had it been 'fixed' by relaxing what counts as a citation, it would have been a guard that stopped guarding.
